record.original_question: Let S be a finite set of rational primes, and let X(S) be the set of rational numbers x in Q such that both x and 1−x are S-units. The source asks for lower bounds on the size of X(S), or on the maximum of |X(S)| over all sets S with |S|=s. Does there exist a lower bound that grows faster than any polynomial in s?

evidence.quote: If S is a finite set of rational primes, let X(S) denote the set of rational numbers x ∈ Q such that both x and 1−x are S-units, and denote by N(s) the maximum of the cardinalities |X(S)| as S ranges through all finite sets of primes with |S| = s.
Problem: Is there a lower bound for |X(S)| (or for the maximum of the cardinalities |X(S)| ranging over sets S with |S| = s) which grows more than polynomially in s?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $S$ of rational primes, a nonzero rational number is called an $S$-unit if every prime appearing (with nonzero exponent) in its factorization belongs to $S$. Define
$$X(S) = \{ x \in \mathbb{Q} : x \text{ and } 1-x \text{ are both } S\text{-units}\},$$
and let
$$N(s) = \max_{|S|=s} |X(S)|,$$
where the maximum is taken over all finite sets $S$ of rational primes of cardinality $s$.

Determine whether there exists a lower bound for $N(s)$ that grows faster than every polynomial in $s$; that is, does there exist a function $f(s)$ with $f(s)/s^k \to \infty$ as $s \to \infty$ for every fixed $k \ge 1$, such that $N(s) \ge f(s)$ for all sufficiently large $s$?
artifact.status_search_result: Erdős, Stewart and Tijdeman (Compositio Math. 66 (1988), 37–56) proved that there exist arbitrarily large sets $S$ of $s$ primes for which the $S$-unit equation $x+y=1$ has at least $\exp((4+o(1))(s/\log s)^{1/2})$ solutions, which grows faster than every polynomial in $s$. This gives an affirmative answer to the question. Konyagin–Soundararajan and Evertse–Moree–Stewart–Tijdeman later refined and generalized such bounds.

status_evidence.title: Some diophantine equations with many solutions
status_evidence.snippet: Erdős, Stewart, Tijdeman, Compositio Math. 66 (1988), 37–56, proving exp((4+o(1))(s/log s)^{1/2}) solutions for S-unit equations.
status_evidence.claim: A superpolynomial (in fact, sub-exponential) lower bound for the number of solutions to x+y=1 in S-units is established, answering the question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Many solutions to the S-unit equation a+1=c
status_evidence.snippet: There are arbitrarily large sets S of s primes for which the S-unit equation a+1=c has at least exp(s^{1/4}/log s) solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work (Konyagin–Soundararajan and others) further confirms superpolynomial growth.
